title: Which queue did the task leave?
hook: A task can leave a toy mental queue by being recorded elsewhere; completion is separate.

knows: basic arithmetic and how to compare two stated rules
doesNotKnow: how to track offloaded commitments separately from completed commitments

misconception: Moving a task out of an in-head queue means the task has been completed.
objective: Track offloaded commitments separately from completed commitments.

claims.text: Original stipulated toy: Fixed eight-task initial queue; no new tasks; transfers remove from this queue but do not complete tasks or delete the external record. Exact feedback inputs [{"label": "No transfers", "values": [8, 0, 0, 3]}, {"label": "Two transfers/round", "values": [8, 0, 2, 3]}]; second author arithmetic check A=8, B=2. No transfers leaves {A}; recording two per round leaves {B}. Transferred tasks remain pending on another list.
claims.source: EDD-010-books-100-models.md formula; this brief fixes invented inputs, not sampled people or measured outcomes. Independent arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck. All displayed labels, hook and prediction premises are scenario conventions. Round only display to two decimals when necessary.

claims.text: Does it hold up? A smaller tracked queue does not prove reduced cognitive load or completed work.
claims.source: Scope boundary: a deterministic toy establishes only the disclosed arithmetic. Book-specific empirical evidence has not been assessed; source-access hold remains. No invented study, effect size or replication verdict.
